spec_match.rationale: DBSC's real surface is the HTTP header protocol, which a static page cannot run; the page says so up front in a labelled note and models the exact protocol roles with real SubtleCrypto ECDSA P-256 sign/verify, but no server route exercises the true Sec-Session header exchange.

interactive.rationale: Seven controls drive real generateKey/sign/verify calls through the register, refresh, protected-call, steal, replay-refresh, replay-call, and reset paths, each writing distinct server-log rows.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The lede's promise — stolen cookie passes without DBSC, fails the proof-of-possession refresh with it — is exactly what the log demonstrates.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers refresh-before-register, unknown session, expired session, empty-signature verification failure, cookie eviction after failed proof, and post-eviction 401.

references.rationale: Feature page, sibling protocol walkthrough, W3C DBSC explainer, and the ChromeStatus entry are all linked.

conformance.rationale: The immutable feature suite (not edited) leans on adjacent baseline surfaces (typeof fetch, Headers, isSecureContext, cookieStore, navigator.credentials) plus one honest negative (no DeviceBoundSession global); defensible for a header-protocol feature with no JS surface, but dbsc-fetch-still-works cannot meaningfully fail — noted for a future human-authored strengthening, not changed here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless-Chrome CDP run 2026-08-16 drove the full seven-step sequence: register bound a session and set the cookie, legit refresh verified the signature (+10s), protected call returned 200, the stolen-cookie refresh failed verification and evicted the cookie, the attacker call returned 401, and reset cleared all state; zero console errors, zero failed requests; full-page screenshot read.

telemetry_health.rationale: No showcaseTelemetry asserts on the signature-verifies and signature-invalid branches, which are the page's two core contracts.

design_system.rationale: Shared variables only; emerald/rose/blue log rows on paper all clear AA; attacker card border uses rose with black text.

accessibility.rationale: All controls are native labelled buttons with visible focus, but the server log has no aria-live/role=log, so outcome rows — the entire point of each click — are not announced, and log rows are prepended which further confuses reading order for AT.

openQuestions.title: Make the server log an accessible live region
openQuestions.detail: Give #log role=log (or aria-live=polite) with an accessible name, and consider appending rather than prepending (or setting aria-relevant) so screen readers announce each verification outcome in a sensible order.

openQuestions.title: Assert the two core contracts via telemetry
openQuestions.detail: Add showcaseTelemetry asserts for legit-refresh verification success and attacker-refresh verification failure so production telemetry catches a SubtleCrypto or logic regression.

guidanceConsulted.query: review pass: accessible live output, honest capability fallbacks, keyboard operability for existing concept demo
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Verify semantic controls, live-region announcements for async state, visible focus, and honest unsupported states rather than fake success.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review-only critique (no frontend change shipped with it): the rubric's accessibility and runtime_evidence scores applied this guidance as the review bar; the page itself was not modified.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Headless-Chrome CDP drive of the page's primary controls on 2026-08-16 with console/network capture.

summary: Strong, honestly-labelled protocol simulation backed by real SubtleCrypto: the full legit and attacker sequences verified headlessly with clean console. Actionable gaps are the un-announced log region and missing telemetry asserts; the immutable suite's one unfalsifiable baseline check is noted for human strengthening.
